I refactored the core and the supporting code.

[InsertionSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSort.java:5) now pushes more responsibility into private helpers: `Range` owns range creation/validation, comparator null checks go through one `requireComparator(...)`, and array copying is centralized in `copyOf(...)`. That removes a chunk of repeated boilerplate from the generic overloads without changing the public API.

I also tightened the caller side. [InsertionSortDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortDemo.java:3) now reuses a shared string-length comparator, and [InsertionSortSelfTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/035_insertion_sort/InsertionSortSelfTest.java:4) now uses typed array assertions and boolean assertion helpers instead of comparing formatted strings, which makes the tests less brittle and more precise.
